{{Quote|Be careful. They're very poisonous.|[[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]]|<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref>}}
'''Kouhuns''' were vermiform arthropods with segmented bodies, roughly thirty centimeters long, from the jungle [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Indoumodo/Legends|Indoumodo]] in [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]]. Small, silent, and fast, kouhuns were capable of delivering a fatal and quick-acting [[Neurotoxin/Legends|neurotoxin]] through their bite, as well as a nonfatal but nonetheless painful sting from their tails. Kouhuns were white in color, though they also existed in reddish-brown and black varieties.

Kouhuns could survive in almost any environment except extreme cold. On their homeworld, they nested in hollow trees and hunted creatures the size of [[Dog/Legends|dogs]]. Though omnivorous, kouhuns were predatory, detecting their prey by its body heat and then attacking it, often choosing between prey simply on the basis of which victim was closest. They were aggressive creatures, but could be scared away by attackers, though they turned to fight when cornered.

Because of their many advantages for covert killings, kouhuns were a favored weapon of [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]]. They would be starved so that they would attack immediately upon being released, then infiltrated into a victim's home via a [[Droid/Legends|droid]], package, or even by slipping through tight spaces such as open windows or ducts. Kouhun nests, spawned by kouhuns who had escaped from assassins, could be found on a number of worlds from the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] to the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core]], including [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|The kouhun teaches us that senseless savagery is the province of animals, not men.|Veradun's father|<ref name="TTL">{{InsiderCite|124|The Old Republic: The Third Lesson}}</ref>}}
[[File:Kouhun.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A kouhun]]
Kouhuns were pale, centipedelike arthropods<ref name="TotG" /> approximately thirty centimeters in length. Silent<ref name="NEGAS" /> and fast,<ref name="TotG" /> kouhuns could administer via a bite from their mouth pincers a nerve toxin both fast-acting and fatal to almost all mammalian species,<ref name="NEGAS" /> and which in most intelligent species created symptoms resembling a heart attack or another natural manner of [[Death/Legends|death]].<ref name="TotG" /> Their second means of administering poison was a tail stinger, which injected a painful but nonlethal dose;<ref name="NEGAS" /> once this was administered, incapacitating the prey, the kouhun could go to work on its victim with its mandibles.<ref name="FF">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 124|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 124]]</ref> To consume their prey, kouhuns released their saliva,<ref name="S&V Collection 31">[[Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection 31|''Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection'' 31]]</ref> which contained a chemical that broke down the prey's flesh into a digestible liquid. If multiple kouhuns set upon a victim, they would leave nothing behind but bones and a stain.<ref name="FF" /> Kouhuns would even attack prey if they were not hungry, acting on their killing instincts.<ref name="TTL" />

The body of the kouhun was segmented, each segment containing a pair of legs, with which they were capable of scaling sheer surfaces.<ref name="RCR" /> The carapace of the kouhun was often naturally white, though they could be fed dyes to change their color;<ref name="TotG" /> some kouhuns, however, were naturally reddish brown or glossy black. The head of the kouhun had a stinging tongue, measuring from four to ten centimeters in length,<ref name="RCR" /> as well as the creature's mandibles and its black eyes.<ref name="TTL" /> Kouhuns came in two varieties, one with a larger segmented body and more pronounced tail stinger than the other.<ref name="NEGAS" />

While they originated on a jungle [[Planet/Legends|world]],<ref name="TotG" /> kouhuns could survive in almost any climate except extreme cold. They could even be found deep underground in damp subterranean caverns.<ref name="RCR" /> Sand worked as an artificial habitat for the creatures; they would remain burrowed and hidden under it until they detected prey.<ref name="TTL" />

==Behavior and intelligence==
[[File:Kouhun-hd.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Two kouhuns climbing onto [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala's]] bed]]
In the wild in the jungles of [[Indoumodo/Legends|Indoumodo]], kouhuns lived in large hollow trees, hunting creatures the size of [[Dog/Legends|dogs]] that nested in crevices within the trees. Kouhuns were attracted to warmth, and they used this sense to locate their victims,<ref name="TotG" /> often targeting simply the nearest warm-blooded creature. Though possessed of a predatory nature, kouhuns were, in fact, omnivorous.<ref name="RCR" /> While aggressive, they could also be timid on occasion; light made them freeze or attempt to hide, and when attacked they fled or hid. When cornered, however, kouhuns would fight back.<ref name="TotG" /> Before they attacked, kouhuns were known to rear up and hiss.<ref name="AOTCn">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref> They had a level of awareness almost akin to [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitivity]], with which they could avoid security systems.<ref name="FF" /> Kouhuns could also use cover to their advantage to sneak up on their prey.<ref name="LF">{{LivingForce|Jigsaw: Portrait of the Artist as a Young Rodian}}</ref> Handling them was dangerous, requiring a container to hold them; if they escaped, they would regard their handler as a threat and attack it. Barely intelligent, kouhuns were classified as vermin.<ref name="RCR" />

==History==
In the time of the [[Great Galactic War]], the [[Veradun's adoptive father|adoptive father]] of [[Darth Malgus]] kept kouhuns as part of his menagerie. He used them as an illustrative lesson for his son, comparing the controlled nature of man with the mindless killing of the kouhun.<ref name="TTL" />

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]] was given two kouhuns by her colleague [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] to [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala/Legends|assassinate]] [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Wesell sent them to [[Naboo Queen (restaurant)|Amidala's apartment]] in an [[ASN courier droid/Legends|ASN courier droid]], which bypassed Amidala's window security, cut a hole into the window, and released the creatures inside. Dropping below the security scanners covering the floor, the kouhuns made their way up Amidala's bed. When the senator's [[Droid/Legends|droid]] security, [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], detected something and turned on its lights, scanning the room, the kouhuns froze. Once the droid went dark, they crawled up to where the senator slept. Before they could kill her, however, Amidala's [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] guard [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] sensed the danger, ran into the room, and sliced them apart with his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]].<ref name="AOTC" />

[[Thook Lafrell]], [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] to the [[Slavery/Legends|slaver]] [[Gomalo]], used kouhuns in the city of [[Tolea Biqua]] on [[Genarius]]<ref name="LF" /> in around [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]].<ref name="20 BBY">The ''[[Living Force Campaign Guide]]'' states that the [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|''Living Force'']] campaign is set one [[Standard year/Legends|year]] after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], an event that is dated to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. As the ''Living Force'' adventure ''[[Below the Belt: Philology|Philology]]'' [[Cularin's disappearance|moved]] the campaign forward ten years to the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], and the adventure ''[[Night Eyes: Night's Homecoming|Night's Homecoming]]'' established that by Year 4 of the campaign over a year had elapsed since the events of ''Philology'', ''[[Jigsaw: Portrait of the Artist as a Young Rodian|Portrait of the Artist as a Young Rodian]]'' can therefore be dated to circa [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]].</ref> After abducting [[Ezra Du'Re]], an agent of the [[Cularin Office of Public Safety]], from a warehouse in the city, Lafrell left behind a number of kouhuns to attack anyone who investigated the scene of the crime. To provide the creatures cover from which to attack, Lafrell left assorted debris scattered across the floor.<ref name="LF" />

==Kouhuns in the galaxy==
[[File:Jarred_Kouhuns.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Zam Wesell receives a pair of kouhuns.]]
Kouhuns were native to the jungle planet Indoumodo,<ref name="TotG" /> in [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]].<ref name="NEGAS" /> Some offworld specimens were found in zoos or poison research facilities, but the vast majority of kouhuns off Indoumodo were in the possession of [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]]. Poor and run-down districts of urban worlds, including Coruscant, were sometimes home to breeding colonies of kouhuns, which traced their origins to escapees from assassins' cages.<ref name="TotG" /> They were found in large numbers on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] worlds of [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], and [[Gamorr/Legends|Gamorr]], as well as [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] such as [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]].<ref name="RCR" />

Assassins found kouhuns useful for their small size, swift motion, and deadly poison.<ref name="TotG" /> A kouhun could be easily passed through security&mdash;<ref name="NEGAS" />carried on one's person, transported by droid, mailed in a package to the target&mdash;<ref name="TotG" />and was nearly untraceable back to the assassin.<ref name="NEGAS" /> They could enter a dwelling through small apertures, such as ducts or windows, whereupon they would home in on a victim's body heat and kill it with their poison.<ref name="TotG" /> Assassins often starved their kouhuns beforehand to spur them to attack the victims.<ref name="NEGAS" /> They sometimes dyed a kouhun the dominant color of the environment that it was intended to infiltrate.<ref name="TotG" /> Criminals also sometimes used kouhuns as traps, leaving them where their enemies would be expected to tread and scattering debris across the floor to give the creatures cover to strike from.<ref name="LF" /> A synthetic neurotoxin known as [[kouhunin]] was developed based on the venom of the kouhun.<ref name="3-D">''[[Star Wars: Darth Vader: A 3-D Reconstruction Log]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Kouhun_Concept.jpg|thumb|right|180px|A near-final kouhun concept]]
Kouhuns, known during production as "assassin bugs,"<ref name="AOTC DVD">{{Film|II}} DVD commentary</ref> were created by [[George Lucas]] for [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']]. His instructions to the design team were to create a [[Wikipedia:centipede|centipedelike creature]] that could inject poison into its victims.<ref name="Art">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones]]''</ref> However, the designs underwent a number of variants, some more spider-like, a number exploring the idea of transparent skin that could show poison coursing underneath. One, with a larger tail stinger, was almost used as a final design and was used in [[Hasbro]]'s action figure scale rendition of the kouhuns.<ref name="DB">{{DB|creature|kouhun|kouhun}}</ref> This was later [[canon]]ized as a separate variation of kouhun in ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''.

For their realization in ''Attack of the Clones'', the kouhuns were computer-generated. To animate them, a technique called "procedural animation" was used, in which the creature's body was first animated to move down a path, then all the legs were animated separately so they would make contact with the ground in a realistic fashion.<ref name="AOTC DVD" /> The sounds of the kouhuns were created by [[Wikipedia:Foley (filmmaking)|foley]] artists [[Dennie Thorpe]] and [[Jana Vance]] by squishing the inside of a [[Wikipedia:Grapefruit|grapefruit]], while the leg sounds were created by running a stick up and down a ridged metal surface.<ref name="Films">"Films Are Not Released, They Escape"&mdash;[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] DVD</ref>
